[1] The petitioner herein seeks for modification of the Award dated 29.01.2015 passed in the LAQ Case No.
14 / 2012 in respect of the land bearing Survey Nos. 599 and 581 of Village - May, Ta. Bhachau, Dist.
Kachchh with the contention that the name of the petitioner, who is one of the co-owners of the aforesaid plots has not been included in the said Award.
[2] The prayer has been made to issue direction to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10133/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/07/2024 undefined Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada Yojana Unit - 1,

sentences.text: [ 3 ] It is stated in the writ petition that the petitioner along with the other four persons had purchased the lands in question vide Registered Sale Deed No. 455 / 1987 dated 11.08.1987 and an entry in the Revenue Record was mutated vide Mutation Entry No. 1984 dated 21.06.2008, which was ultimately certified on 09.09.2008.

[4] We may note that the copy of the sale deed has not been brought on record, though the Revenue Record showing the Mutation Entry has been appended as Annexure - B indicating the name of the petitioner therein.

[5] It is stated that various parcels of the land in question have been acquired by acquisition notifications published in the year 2012 and 2013 under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and final award was passed on 29.01.2015.

The contention is that the Special Land Acquisition Officer erroneously missed out the name of the petitioner in the final award, though he was the rightful owner of the land in question.
[6] Be that as it may, suffice it to note that the award passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10133/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/07/2024 undefined only adjudicates the compensation pertaining to the acquired land.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Act, 1894 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10133/2024
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The rights and interests of the persons interested in the land are not adjudicated under Section 11.

As far as the apportionment of compensation is concerned, the same is guided by the provisions contained in Sections 29 and 30 in Part IV of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which state that where there are several persons interested, if such persons agree in the apportionment of the compensation, the particulars of such apportionment shall be specified in the Award and as between such persons, the award shall be conclusive evidence of the correctness of the apportionment.

However, in case of any dispute as to the apportionment of the amount of compensation settled under Section 11, or any part thereof, or as to the person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the Collector shall have to refer the dispute to the decision of the Competent Court.

[7] Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, further, mandates the Collector to issue notice to the persons interested at the time of making of the Award, so as to enable them to appear before the Collector and file evidence for determination of true area and value of the land and apportionment of compensation among the person interested.

In Paragraph '3.16' of the writ petition, a bald assertion has been NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10133/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/07/2024 undefined made by the petitioner that no notice was ever served upon the petitioner and the petitioner was not aware about any such proceedings.
The further contention is that the petitioner has made a request for modification of the Award, which has not been looked into.
And hence, this petition.

[8] Noticing the above provisions, we are of the considered view that in absence of other co-owners of the land in question being impleaded herein, it is not possible for us to issue any positive direction.

sentences.text: [9] However, an opportunity is granted to the petitioner to approach the Collector by writing a representation along with the copy of this order to make a statement with regard to his right, title and interest in the land in question along with the necessary documents to establish the same.

On such application being received before the Collector with the period of two weeks from today, the same shall be forwarded to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada Yojana, Unit - 1, Bhachau for adjudication of the claim of the petitioner for apportionment of compensation determined under the Award dated 29.01.2015 and the Supplementary Award dated 07.03.2018 (which was passed by applying 'Factor-2' for a rural area).
[10] A notice and opportunity shall be given to all other NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/10133/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/07/2024 undefined co-owners of the land in question by the Special Land Acquisition Officer before passing the final order determining the claim of the petitioner for disbursement of the compensation by apportionment thereof, as per his share in the land in question.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer has to adjudicate keeping in mind the provisions of Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

A reasoned and speaking order, strictly in accordance with law, shall be passed preferably within the period of two months from the date of receipt of the representation, under due intimation to the petitioner.

[11] The prayer made by the petitioner before the Land Acquisition Officer for making correction by invoking Section 13 (A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is found misconceived, inasmuch as the issue raised by the petitioner is about his entitlement to receive compensation, which does not fall within the scope of clerical or typographical error in the Award.
With the above, the writ petition stands disposed of.

(SUNITA AGARWAL, CJ ) (PRANAV TRIVEDI,J) SAHIL S. RANGER Gandhi Hirji Ranchhod vs State Of Gujarat on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95657569/
